title: Pilot MEDIUM — Variant inactive sales invariant
description: Execute the first real Item 8 MEDIUM-risk pilot by closing a catalog domain invariant gap: an inactive variant must never remain sales-enabled. The change is intentionally bounded to VariantAggregate behavior plus focused regression evidence and does not touch pricing, inventory, payment, auth, database, API contracts, dependencies, workflows, or canonical roadmap state.

why_medium: This task changes production catalog business logic rather than tests or documentation only.
The invariant controls whether an inactive product variant can remain marked as sales-enabled, so regression could affect storefront/admin sellability semantics.
The change is small, reversible, deterministic, and isolated to a non-sensitive Catalog domain aggregate.
why_not_high: No payment, pricing, inventory, authentication, authorization, finance, irreversible database migration, destructive operation, security policy, GitHub workflow, ruleset, or protected-main setting is changed.
The production path is outside current Project Map HIGH sensitive zones.
Human and Security gates are therefore not required unless deterministic classification escalates.

external_gate_evidence.rule: MEDIUM-risk pilot requires exact-artifact ACTIVE LOCK, independent REVIEW PASS and deterministic verification evidence. Security and Human gates are not required unless risk escalates to HIGH.

acceptance_criteria.description: Transitioning a sales-enabled variant to inactive automatically leaves the resulting variant sales-disabled and emits the updated event with sales_enabled=false.
An explicit attempt to keep or enable sales while the resulting variant status is inactive fails closed with VARIANT_INACTIVE and does not mutate state, version, or event history.
Reactivating an inactive variant does not silently resume sales; sales may only become enabled when the resulting status is active and the caller explicitly requests it.
Exact-head canonical verification passes with no regression in the repository test suite.
The PR changes exactly the four authorized pilot paths and makes no payment, pricing, inventory, auth, database, API contract, dependency, workflow, telemetry, or canonical roadmap mutation.

Deterministic task classification is MEDIUM because the production catalog domain path matches the task risk rule; independent Review and verification are required while Security and Human gates remain not required unless classification escalates.
The pilot merges only through the protected canonical Merge Policy workflow and is followed by exact-SHA post-merge verification before MEDIUM pilot completion is claimed.

No token-usage value is invented for LOW or MEDIUM when an authoritative provider/runtime usage record is unavailable; absence of telemetry remains explicit rather than being converted into synthetic calibration data.
